question: Do third States enjoy any fishing rights within the Exclusive Economic Zone of another State?

options.A: Third States may never have access to fisheries within another State's EEZ
options.B: Third States are free to fish within another EEZ, except from certain designated areas
options.C: When the coastal State cannot harvest the 'total allowable catch', the coastal State is to give other State access to that surplus with priority to be given to developing and land-locked States
options.D: The coastal State must share all of its fish resources with all other States
options.E: Third States have access to fisheries within its EEZ only during a specific season
options.F: The coastal State is to give access to fisheries within its EEZ only to States with which it has diplomatic relations
options.G: Third States have unlimited fishing rights within the EEZ of any State
options.H: Third States can only fish within another State's EEZ with a special permit
options.I: The coastal State is to give access to fisheries within its EEZ only to neighbouring States
options.J: Third States can only fish within another State's EEZ if they have a mutual agreement
